t: Introduction and overview — F-16 Fighting Falcon
name: Introduction and overview — F-16 Fighting Falcon — aircraft record
title: Introduction and overview — F-16 Fighting Falcon
description: Introduction and overview of the F-16 Fighting Falcon: What this aircraft is, its role, and why it matters in aviation history. The F-16 Fighting Falcon is a single-engine multirole fighter built by General Dynamics (now Lockheed Martin), first flown in 1974 and in service since 1978. About 4,600 have been built, making it one of the most-produced modern jet fighters. It was the first production fighter with a fly-by-wire control system, a bubble canopy for 360-degree visibility, and a side-mounted control stick. Baseline facts: Single-engine multirole fighter; first flight 1974; ~4,600 built by General Dynamics/Lockheed Martin..
how_it_works: Wings generate lift from airflow; the engine provides thrust; control surfaces and fly-by-wire or mechanical controls steer the aircraft in three axes.
key_points: F-16 Fighting Falcon: What this aircraft is, its role, and why it matters in aviation history.
Single-engine multirole fighter; first flight 1974; ~4,600 built by General Dynamics/Lockheed Martin.
Key figure: Top speed Mach 2.02 (1,320 mph); powered by one Pratt & Whitney F100 or General Electric F110 turbofan.
